newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SINGAPORE NOON SHARES SLIDE ON FUNDS, REGIONALS.
newsitem.headline: SINGAPORE NOON SHARES SLIDE ON FUNDS, REGIONALS.

text.p: Singapore shares fell sharply on Monday morning to sit precariously on the brink of the year's low due to heavy institutional selling.
Dealers said confidence eroded in a local bourse beset with concerns that local and foreign share tranches might be merged.
"Foreign tranches of banks and blue chips are under pressure. After last week's uncertainty, fund managers are very cautious," a dealer with a foreign institution said.
SPH foreign lost Singapore 40 cents to S$12.60. OCBC foreign shed 20 cents to s$13.60.
By the lunch break, the Straits Times Industrials Index (STII) had plunged 1.55 percent to 1,913.87, down 30.05 points.
This was flirting with the previous year low of 1,913.55, a break of which would next test support at 1,900 points.
Retail sellers were also seen quick to sell down Malaysian over-the-counter shares, hit by the weak market across the Causeway, dealers said.
The UOB OTC index lost 20.90 points to 1,009.21 at noon.
Hogging the actives was newly-listed Hotung Investments HOTU.SI, which hit a high of US$0.54 on its debut before dropping back to US$0.49, up from its IPO price of US0.26.
Profit taking brought down Hongkong Land, which fell US0.14 to US$3.28 after speculation last week that it might be up for takeover drove the issue higher in active dealings.
Hotel Properties, despite news it would develop hotels and resorts worldwide with Hard Rock Cafe on Friday, failed to inspire interest.
It fell to a new low of S$2.14 before inching back to S$2.17, down seven cents.
